blindSummary:
This is a progressive destination in its region — the first in the region to legalise same-sex marriage (2019), the government is funding a multi-year programme to double gender-neutral public bathrooms by 2029, and a trans march in the capital drew 3,000 participants in 2025. There are no documented severe incidents (no mob violence, trans-tourist rape, or organised dating-app predation).

The main gaps are stagnation in legal-gender-recognition reform — a 2008 ministry order still requires sex-reassignment surgery to change one's gender marker (blocking an estimated 90% of trans people, with only case-by-case court exceptions), and the government has been vacillating on reform — and a rising anti-gender discourse movement that has produced online waves of hostility. A trans woman was outed during a police identity inspection (a documented case), and the capital has held a vigil for victims of anti-trans violence.

For a visitor, bathrooms are unrestricted (and being proactively expanded to gender-neutral), there is no criminalisation, and border/immigration poses no trans-specific friction. The capital's city government has trans-friendly service guidelines.
blindOutOfScope: No trans-specific travel advisory; earthquake and major-storm risks affect all travellers.
blindSourceSummaries: Online news magazine (Feb 2026): commentary on the ongoing struggle for self-ID - the 2008 executive order requiring sex-reassignment surgery to change legal gender blocks an estimated 90% of trans people from obtaining identity documents that match; every ID-requiring aspect of daily life (clinics, airport security) becomes a potential site of distress and discrimination; the health ministry has recognised gender self-determination as a human right since 2013.

Online news magazine (Jan 2026): the government continued to vacillate on transgender rights in 2025 amidst continued transphobia - no tangible policy change on abolishing the surgery requirement or expanding assisted reproduction; pending conscription-criteria changes could actively harm trans people; anti-gender movement activity is rising, with organisations aligned to a large foreign country's current anti-trans policies and a small political party calling for a 'two genders' constitutional position.

National daily (Aug 2024): the environment ministry will invest 280 million units of local currency over four years to double gender-neutral public bathrooms nationwide (623 to 1,246 by 2029); of trans and gender-neutral survey respondents reporting discrimination, 17% occurred in public restrooms or changing rooms.

A national news agency (Nov 2025): an LGBTQ+ rights group reports that only 5 of 149 government-listed all-gender public toilets in this country met the required standards, including clear signage admitting all genders.

Independent media outlet (Nov 2024): analysis of the wave of anti-gender discourse here - rising anti-gender movement activity and its political context.

Public broadcaster (Aug 2024): a court in the capital denied a transgender woman's request to change the gender marker on her government ID without requiring surgery or a psychological evaluation; the supporting rights group says they will likely appeal.

Legal news dispatch (Nov 2025): the 7th annual transgender march in the capital drew an estimated 3,000 people despite rain, with international participants; calls for an end to discrimination against trans people as the rights debate continues.

LGBT travel-and-resources site: 'one of the region's most progressive places for LGBT rights, and certainly the most liberal where its language is spoken'; notes same-sex adoption was regularised for parents here on May 16, 2023; listings of organisations, bars, spas and venues across 12 cities.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2008 surgery-required gender-marker order and the stalled reform are resident-facing; the outing case concerned a resident.
blindTangential: Same-sex marriage legal since 2019 — relevant to trans visitors travelling with partners.
